cards.note: Cereus hildmannianus is a species of cactus from southern South America. Its distribution is uncertain but probably includes Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina.

It is native to several provinces including Jujuy, Tucumán, La Rioja, San Juan, Catamarca and Salta provinces in northwestern Argentina, and is the eponymous cactus of Los Cardones National Park in Salta Province.

Armatocereus matucanensis is a species of Armatocereus from Ecuador and Peru. There's many species of Armatocereus, I just picked the one that was easier to find and identify. They generally look very similar and are found in the same places so it's not that important.

Myrtillocactus Geometrizans is a species of cactus in the genus Myrtillocactus, native to central and northern Mexico. It is especially abundant in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo, and much more rarely Guanajuato.

Eulychnia acida, commonly known as cactus ácido or copao, is a cactus species endemic to Chile, where it is primarily distributed in the semi-arid regions of the country. Its range includes: Atacama Region, Coquimbo Region,and Valparaíso Region.
Pachycereus weberi is widespread in the Mexican states of Puebla, Guerrero, Morelos, Hidalgo and Oaxaca at altitudes of 600 to 1,500 m.

The distribution area of Xiquexique Tuberculatus extends from the northwest to the northeast of the Brazilian state of Bahia and extends into the state of Pernambuco. It can easily be confused with its brother the Xiquexique Gounellei - X. Tuberculatus has thinner shoots with less ribs, and shorter spines.
The species originates from Mexico (Guerrero, Michoacán, Oaxaca, southern Puebla). It will almost always place you somewhere in Oaxaca, usually central in the state.
There is two main subspecies of this cactus, they are hard to tell apart through streetview imagery so I'll treat them as the same cactus. It's found in south Ecuador, Perú, and Bolivia.
This species is mostly found in the dry regions of Colombia (mostly in Guajira, Tatacoa desert) and the ABC islands of the Dutch Caribbean (only Curaçao is in geoguessr).
Pachycereus pringlei is a species of large cactus native to northwestern Mexico, in the states of Baja California, Baja California Sur, and Sonora.
Cylindropuntia fulgida is a cholla cactus native to Sonora and the Southwestern United States.
Cereus jamacaru, known as mandacaru or cardeiro is a cactus native to central and eastern Brazil.

N. arequipensis is endemic to Peru, where it is found in Arequipa, Ayacucho, Cajamarca, Huancavelica, Lima, Lambayique, Piura and sometimes other regions. It commonly grows in rocky coastal habitats, desert scrub and inter-Andean valleys.

Opuntia quimilo is a species of Prickly Pear belonging to the Cactaceae family. It is found in north-central Argentina and is widespread in Bolivia. The Opuntia (Prickly Pears) have been spread out through the world and they all look very similar, but within each country that has them, it is often possible to regionguess when you see them.

This species is found mostly in Mexico, mainly in Sonora and southern Baja California and Northern Sinaloa. It is also found in the Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument in southern Arizona and ocasionally elsewhere in southern Arizona.

Similar story to the Armatocereus in Perú. This cactus has many species but they are all found in north-eastern Brazil and generally look very similar. I just chose to include the P. Pachycladus in the map.
Stenocereus queretaroensis is a species of cactus from Mexico, mostly in the states of Querétaro, Guanajuato and Jalisco. It is cultivated for its fruit.
This cactus is really rare to see in Streetview since the area where it is commonly found lacks coverage, but if you see it, you're most likely be on the 37D in Michoacán.

Echinopsis Chiloensis occur along the coast and in the coastal cordillera of Chile (North-Central Valley of Chile) in the regions of Maule, O'Higgins, Metropolitana, Valparaíso and Coquimbo, from Talca to Valle del Elqui.

The Saguaro is endemic to the Sonoran Desert and is found primarily in western Sonora in Mexico, and in western Arizona in the US. Elevation is a limiting factor to its environment, as the saguaro is sensitive to extended frost or cold temperatures.

Stetsonia coryne is distributed in high-altitude arid regions, such as the deserts and dry forest (Gran Chaco) of northwestern Argentina, as well as in Bolivia, Paraguay, and the Brazilian state of Mato Grosso do Sul.

Cylindropuntia imbricata is a cactus found in the Southwestern United States and northern Mexico, including some cooler regions in comparison to many other cacti. It occurs primarily in the arid regions of the Southwestern United States in the states of Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas, New Mexico, Arizona, Colorado, and Nevada.

Xiquexique Gounellei is widespread in northeastern Brazil in the Caatinga vegetation. It can easily be confused with its brother the Xiquexique Tuberculatus - X. Gounellei has thicker shoots with more ribs and longer spines.
